source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Teaching relaxation and breathing techniques, and addressing anxiety as a legitimate component of the overall symptom experience, alongside physical disease management","B":"Ignoring the anxiety component of this particular cycle entirely, focusing only on addressing the client's physical respiratory symptoms","C":"A cycle that is generally considered to lack any established management approach that nurses can actually offer to affected clients","D":"Assuming that the client's anxiety is not a genuine, real physiological experience worth acknowledging as part of their overall plan of care"}}
source_row.rationale: Addressing the dyspnea-anxiety cycle includes teaching relaxation and breathing techniques, and addressing anxiety as a legitimate component of the overall symptom experience (since anxiety and dyspnea can genuinely worsen each other physiologically), managed alongside, not instead of, physical disease management.
source_row.source_name: American Thoracic Society — Dyspnea-Anxiety Cycle Management
source_row.stem: A nurse recognizes that a client with chronic respiratory disease may experience a cycle in which dyspnea triggers anxiety, which in turn worsens the sensation of breathlessness. Addressing this cycle includes:
